title: Thought, speech and action in the Essence's own thought: the world planned down to the last nail
overview: The thought, speech and action within thought of the earlier chapters are now found in G-d's own thought, in the Essence before the *tzimtzum*. Its action within thought is the *sof maaseh*: the *Aibershter* thought of the world not only as His dwelling, as a person thinks of sitting, but as a chair's designer does, as a separate thing to be built down to the last nut and bolt. Nothing in the world happens by itself, any more than a tree grows in a painting. Every star, every nail and every electron has a name and a place; the steak, the drink and the *Shabbos* chicken were meant for one person, and a story of a yahrtzeit schnapps shows what hangs on it. Speech within that thought is His measuring in advance what will come; thought within thought is *Ana Emloch*, the will to rule. Deeds below reach up to that first thought. Its depth is beyond any number, yet not beyond Him. The rest of the chapter, taught off the tape, carries the three levels down to *Zeir Anpin*; class 218 explains the large *dalet* of *Echad*, the back of *bina*.

sections.title: Action within the essential thought: the world designed as a thing apart, down to every nail
sections.summary: The Essence's own thought has thought, speech and action, and its action is the *sof maaseh*: the *Aibershter* thought of the world not only as His dwelling but as an external thing to be built, every star, atom and nail in its place, as a painter puts on every stroke. So every steak, drink and *Shabbos* chicken is meant for one person.

ובחינת מעשה שבמחשבה העצמית שבעצמות ממש הוא כמו ענין סוף מעשה שעלה במחשבה תחלה
(ודלא כלשון הרמב"ם
בידיעת עצמו יודע את הכל
phrases.en: He knows everything by knowing Himself

phrases.he: אלא מה שיודע את כל ההשתלשלות דאבי"ע בידיעה שחוץ ממנו, היינו בחינת עשיה שבמחשבה, כמו שחושב בציור דבר נבדל,
phrases.en: The *Aibershter* had a *machshava* of the world as if the world is a separate thing.

phrases.he: הגם שאין לך דבר חוץ כו')
phrases.en: Even though there is nothing really outside of Him

blocks.text: In the Essence's own *machshava* (thought), the *maaseh sheb'machshava* (action within thought) is like the *sof maaseh*, the end of the deed that rose first in thought. He is not arguing with the *Rambam* here. It says that **the *Aibershter* had a *machshava* of the world as if the world is a separate thing**.

Still, it is not just what the *Rambam* says. The usual teaching is that in the simple thought a person is not really thinking of the actual house but of himself, of his *taanug* (delight). Here it says no: the *Aibershter* thought of the actual house, which is a different thing.

blocks.title: The chair and its designer
blocks.text:
Before a person thinks of a chair, he does not think of a chair at all. He thinks of sitting, and then looks around for a chair somebody else designed. The designer had to think of an actual chair, not only of the comfort of the sitter: which nuts go where, the bolts and the pieces of wood the sitter never thinks about even while he sits in it. He thought of it as a chair, something apart from the sitting.

So when the *Aibershter* thought of the world, He did not think of it only as His *dira b'tachtonim* (dwelling below). He thought of designing an external thing down to its last detail, the last nut and bolt, the way one thinks of putting together a thing outside oneself.

And **even though there is nothing really outside of Him**, He had a thought as if He were putting together something outside Him. Nothing just happened automatically: the *Aibershter* had to design every tiny detail of the world.

blocks.title: Who is mother nature?
blocks.text:
The shows on the wonders of nature marvel at mother nature. Ask who this mother nature is, she must be a great genius, and they say there is no mother nature: it happens by natural selection, it is inherent in the universe. Give it all the billions of years you like: will a light ray ever evolve that goes round and round instead of straight? No, they say, that is not in nature; it cannot mutate into that. So they too are saying it is built into nature and happens by itself.

What the chapter says is that nothing happens automatically. The bottom line is that the *Aibershter* had to design every little piece of it.

blocks.title: The painting
blocks.text: It is like a story or a painting. In a painting the leaf does not grow out of the branch naturally: the painter painted the leaf, the branch and the earth. Ask how the tree got into the painting, and someone answers that the sun is up in the sky, the ground is below, it must have rained a little earlier in the painting, and so the tree grew. It does not work like that in a painting; the artist had to do it. Nor did he think, "a beautiful scene with a house, a tree and a little kid running around," and poof, the painting came up.

blocks.title: The painting
blocks.text: First he thought of it in terms of himself: the scene came out of a *taanug* he had for it, the feeling of a house, a tree and a little kid running around. Then he had to sit down, and every stroke of the brush on that canvas was put there technically, not emotionally, even though it brings out an emotion.

That is the *maaseh sheb'machshava* of the three levels within thought: thinking how to do a certain thing. To make a piece of clothing, a little contraption or a basket, a person works out what materials he needs, what kind of weave, and how it will all be woven together.

blocks.title: The universe as a weave
blocks.text: The universe is something like a weave; that is why weaving, the *shti va'erev* (warp and woof), is one of the *melachos* (the labors of *Shabbos*). Science got down to quarks, and now string theory has even smaller strings, folding like origami and collapsing on themselves in eleven dimensions, weaving up into the subatomic particles, and strings in time too. They don't realize there are more than eleven dimensions: there are as many as the *Aibershter* wants there to be. So to make the worlds, the *Aibershter* has to place each little dot, each quark, each atom.

blocks.title: The peach tree and the beanstalk
blocks.text: In a painting nothing is there that was not put there. How did that big peach tree get there? A seed was in the ground and it grew? A seed in the ground does not grow on a painting; the artist put every piece there. The same in a cartoon of Jack and the Beanstalk: he puts the bean in the ground, it shoots up, and it is funny, a miracle, it grows so fast. What miracle? Every frame is painted. Nothing is there without the artist knowing exactly where it is and putting it there.

blocks.title: The named nails
blocks.text: This *machshava* is not the thought of how He will sit in the house but of exactly how to make it, what materials, what nails. And it is more intricate than that. A builder does not call his nails by name: he buys a box, and when he is ready to bang one stud into another he takes any nail. The world is not made like that. Each nail has a name and each stud has a name, and if the wrong nail goes into the wrong stud, the whole house falls apart.

blocks.title: Two stars and the flood
blocks.text: So with the stars: "He calls them all by name." It is not that He put a bunch of stars out there. Each star has a name and has to be in its exact location; take it out and a catastrophe could follow. One of the *meforshim* (commentators) says the *Aibershter* brought the *mabul* (the Flood) by taking two stars out of some *mazal* (constellation). How could stars thousands or millions of light years away affect the earth? That is what you think; you don't understand how it works. The *Aibershter* knows which star is which, what each is to do, its kind and its gravitational pulls, all exact, down to the finest detail of the finest atom.

blocks.title: Electron Chaimie and electron Shloimie
blocks.text: The atoms are not interchangeable either; they have names, Chaimie and Shloimie. Science pictures a mass of electrons flying around, interchangeable, as if it does not matter which one is where. Take electron Chaimie, flying around your room, and electron Shloimie over here, and swap them: the charge is the same, an electron is an electron, so nothing should change. It is not true. Chaimie has to be in that exact location and Shloimie in this one. Otherwise the whole mathematics of the universe would change, and the whole universe could collapse on itself because the math would be wrong.

blocks.title: One formula, one Name
blocks.text: String theory is turning up something its people do not understand: that the whole universe could be represented by a single numerical formula. And a name is a number. The names of *Havaya* are *Ayin Beis*, *SaG*, *MaH* and *BaN*: 72, 63, 45 and 52. What does 52 have to do with a name? A name is made of letters, and letters are numbers, mathematical formulas. So it says the heavens are made from the *yud* and the earth from the *heh*, part of the formula of the name *yud ka vav ka*, which includes everything. Like a formula it breaks down into *temuros*, *chilufim* and *miluim* (permutations, exchanges and fillings), and the *miluim* have *miluim*, and the whole thing can be symbolized in that one name.

blocks.title: Electron Chaimie and electron Shloimie
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 217 opens by finishing class 216's explanation of lines 3-5; it reads line 6 only at word 1334.
blocks.text: Swapping the two electrons shows it is not only that a room needs enough electrons for the charge to be right. They think that if one electron stopped existing, others would fill its place; but what happens to their places? For the formula to be exactly right, each nail has to be in its place. Nail one cannot go in the place of nail two; they are not really interchangeable.

blocks.title: The steak meant for him
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 217, still on lines 3-5 before it reads line 6.
blocks.text: By us some things are interchangeable. A waiter in a restaurant does not stop to think which steak was meant for this customer. It is not really true: it was *davka* (precisely) that steak that was meant for him, and he could not eat someone else's. What is the difference which steak he eats? That steak has his *nitzotzos* (sparks).

blocks.title: The schnapps at the yahrtzeit
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 217, still on lines 3-5 before it reads line 6.
blocks.text: The story is with one of the great Rebbes of the Alter Rebbe's time; he thinks the Ruzhiner or the Karliner, or the Berditchever. A man came in with a bottle of vodka for his father's *yahrtzeit* (the anniversary of a passing), said a quick *Kaddish*, put the bottle on the table and turned to run off to work. He was a *proster Yid* (a simple Jew). They held him back: it's your father's *yahrtzeit*, make a *lechaim*, it will be an *aliya* (elevation) for your father, a *tikkun*. Finally they poured him a little schnapps and he drank it straight down. They all shouted: you didn't say the *bracha* (blessing)! What's the difference, he said, if I said the *bracha* or not?

blocks.title: The schnapps at the yahrtzeit
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 217, still on lines 3-5 before it reads line 6.
blocks.text:
Just then the Rebbe walked in and told him a story. In the heavenly court, those on the right and those on the left argued over your father, and it was decided he should go to hell: he did many *mitzvos*, but the sins were bigger. Finally they sent his soul back down, so that you would make a *bracha* over it, raise the *nitzotzos*, and he could go to heaven. His *neshama* (soul) went into wheat plants, and all the way, through the threshing and the vodka plant and the pouring, the bad angels tried to make it get lost and the good angels made sure it came through, until the whole of your father's soul was in that little cup. All you had to do was make a *bracha* over it and drink it. Look what you did instead.

The man fainted. Afterwards he asked the Rebbe for a *tikkun* and became his *chassid*.

blocks.title: The Shabbos chicken
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 217, still on lines 3-5 before it reads line 6.
blocks.text: So a piece of food that comes to a person was designated for him; it is his piece of food. As they say, forty days before, it is designated: there is a certain girl for every man. It is not a bunch of girls, not this one so that one; "plenty of fish in the ocean" does not work. It is already *bashert* (destined), which girl goes to which guy. And not only in marriage. The chicken a person eats this *Shabbos* had to be that chicken; while it was growing it was already his, not one of a million that he happened to get. And for the chicken too, it had to be *davka* him.

blocks.outOfPlace: Class 217 returns to lines 4-5 just before it reads line 6.
blocks.text: So it is with everything. That explains the line that seems to go against what is usually said in *Chassidus*, that **He knows everything by knowing Himself** and there is nothing outside Him. Of course there is nothing outside Him; but He has to plan the world as if it were an actual thing outside Himself.

sections.title: Speech within the essential thought: measuring in advance what will come
sections.summary: The *dibur sheb'machshava* of the Essence is His estimating in Himself what will be in the chain of descent, the engraving of letters, "He said, and it was". Thought is the original idea, speech how it will come out, in general, like *Ana Emloch*, and action the plan of every detail.

phrases.he: ובחינת דבור שבמחשבה העצמית
הוא כמו מה ששיער בעצמו בכח מה שעתיד להיות בהשתלשלות כו'
phrases.en: He was actually *meshaer* exactly how it's going to be, what forces are going to have to come into it.

phrases.he: שזה שנאמר גליף גליפו בטהירו עילאה, חקיקת אותיות בעצמות כו'

blocks.text: The *dibur sheb'machshava* (speech within thought) of the Essence is what He estimated in Himself of what would be in the chain of descent: the engraving of letters in the Essence, *glif glifu*. **He was actually *meshaer* exactly how it's going to be**, what forces would have to come into it.

phrases.he: וכן מה שכתוב כי הוא אמר, במחשבה העצמית, ויהי, ההוא אמר ולא יעשה, על ידי צמצום הראשון כו' וכהאי גוונא
כי כל אמירה הוא בבחינת דבור שבמחשבה הנזכר לעיל
(שלמעלה משמיעת דבור זולתו, כמו הטה אזנך ושמע כו' ויקשב וישמע וכהאי גוונא)

blocks.text: In "He said, and it was", the saying is in the essential thought. *Machshava* is the original thought of the thing, *dibur* how it will come out, *maaseh* the plan of each designated thing. *Dibur* is general, like *Ana Emloch* (I will reign); in the *maaseh sheb'machshava* He works out every detail. Every saying, and the hearing of another's speech in "Incline Your ear and hear": **that's also called *dibur sheb'machshava***.

sections.title: Thought within the essential thought: Ana Emloch, a depth beyond number
sections.summary: Thought within thought is the grasp of the idea itself, *Ana Emloch*, the will to rule. Deeds below reach that first thought, where the *chesed* rose before it was. Its depth is beyond any number, since it holds the name of every nail, and yet He understood it, or it would not work.

phrases.he: ומחשבה שבמחשבה העצמית היינו כמו שמבואר למעלה במחשבת השכלת הענין בצירופים שונים כו'
והוא כאשר עלה ברצונו ומחשבתו אנא אמלוך וכהאי גוונא,
והוא על פי חכמתו ורצונו העצמית כו'
וזהו שאמר והיה העולם, בבחינת מלכות דאין סוף, אנא אמלוך כו'

blocks.text: The *machshava sheb'machshava* (thought within thought) of the Essence is thinking the idea in its various *tzirufim* (combinations): when *Ana Emloch* rose in His will and thought. That is the actual *haskala* (grasp) of the thing, what He wanted; it is its very essence, that He wants to rule.

phrases.he: (ולפי זה מה שנתעורר בחינת חפץ חסד הראשון על ידי מעשה התחתונים כו'
phrases.en: Through the *maasim* downstairs you *meorer* the *chesed* upstairs.

phrases.he: שמחמתו עלה במחשבתו ורצונו כו',
phrases.en: The thing of the *chesed* came up even before the *chesed* itself came up: it came up in the original *machshava*.

phrases.he: הרי הוא מגיע לתחלת התעוררות הרצון במחשבה העצמית וכו')
phrases.en: It goes into the *hisorerus haratzon* in the *machshava ha'atzmis*.

blocks.text: When through the *maasim* (deeds) below a person is *meorer* (arouses) the first *chafetz chesed* (desire for kindness) above, he reaches the original thought, since the *chesed* came up there before the *chesed* itself did. He arouses it all the way up, and so the *chesed* He wanted to happen happens. **It goes into the *hisorerus haratzon* in the *machshava ha'atzmis***: the arousal of the will in the essential thought.

phrases.he: וזה שכתוב נפלאותיך ומחשבותיך אלינו כו' עצמו מספר
phrases.en: There's too much to talk about.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב לתבונתו אין מספר
כי לפי ערך העמקת החכמה והדעת, כן ערך העמקת בחינת המחשבה העצמית בעצמות אור אין סוף,
phrases.en: The *omek* of *machshava* is according to the *omek* of the idea.

phrases.he: כמו מה מאד עמקו מחשבותיך וכנזכר לעיל ודי למבין.

blocks.text: "Your wonders and Your thoughts toward us are too many to tell": **There's too much to talk about**. As "His understanding has no number": **There's no number**. Which number is it, 52 or 45, with which *miluim*? None; it goes higher and higher, up to the *machshava ha'atzmis*, beyond number, because that number would have to include the name of every nail.

Try to think it through, this nail goes here and that nail there, and you cannot; it is past any understanding or number. And yet it is not beyond His understanding. It sounds as if it were beyond anybody's understanding, but it cannot be: had the *Aibershter* not understood it, it would not have worked in the first place. He did understand it, and He made it work like this.

As the depth of wisdom and knowledge, so the depth of the essential thought in the Essence. As was said, **The *omek* of *machshava* is according to the *omek* of the idea**: "How very deep are Your thoughts."

sections.title: The same three levels down the chain to Zeir Anpin (not on tape)
sections.summary: After the first *tzimtzum*, the will and primordial thought of the *Kav*, which sees everything at a glance, also has thought, speech and action, *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*, down through *Adam Kadmon*, *Atik Yomin* and *Arich Anpin* to the thought that clothes the *middos*, called *Leah*, and the thought of *Zeir Anpin*, where a thing can stay in thought and never reach speech. The series has no class on these lines; class 218's recap says only that thought, speech and action go on at every level.

sections.title: The large dalet of Echad: Malchus of tevuna, the back of bina
sections.summary: The large *dalet* of *Echad* is *Malchus* of *tevuna*, the *achoraim* of *Ima*: not the inside of *bina* but its application, at the back of the head like the knot of the head *tefillin*. It is the root of the thought of *Leah*, which counts as speech within thought. Only lines 28-29 are on tape.

phrases.he: והנה על דרך זה יובן בענין ד' רבתי דאחד
שהוא בבחינת מלכות דתבונה שמבחינת אחוריים דאימא כו',
והוא ענין קשר של תפילין של ראש כו' כידוע

blocks.outOfPlace: Class 218 opens by summing up the end of the chapter, which it says was finished already in a class not on tape: thought, speech and action at every level (lines 16-27) and Leah and Malchus of tevuna (apparently lines 30-35). Those lines have no recording, so the recap is placed here, before the class reads lines 28-29.
blocks.text: A summing-up. Thought, speech and action go on at every level. And the thought of *Leah* comes out of the thought of *tevuna* (bina as it is drawn out), which is the inner thing of the *machshava sheb'machshava*. The two are *mamash* almost the same, hard to tell apart, yet *Leah* is called the *dibur sheb'machshava* of the *machshava sheb'machshava*. As the *levush* (garment) of the actual thought of the intellect, it counts as speech: it is a person talking to himself inside his head, though he does not yet plan to say it out loud. And *Malchus* of *tevuna* is the root of *Malchus*.

blocks.question: What does it mean that the large dalet of Echad is Malchus of tevuna, from the achoraim of Ima?
blocks.text: *Malchus* of *tevuna* is the *achoraim* (back) of *Ima*, of *bina*: its end, as in chapter two. It is only the *middos* of *bina*, its *hispashtus* (spreading out), not the real *pnimiyus* (inside) of *bina*. *Bina* in general is the *Chabad* of *bina*, with its *middos* as they are intellectual. *Tevuna* is the *middos* of *bina* as they come out of it: *davka* the application, not the understanding itself but its back.

That is why it is at the back of the head, the *dalet*: not the front of the brain but its back part. *Tevuna* is not the front, the *pnimiyus* of *bina*; it is its tail end, its lower part, its backside. It is not the very *inyan* of *bina*, even though in a way it is.

In a way *tevuna* reaches higher than *bina* and gets you more, but it is still not the real thing; it is just a tail. So the Americans have reached far greater heights with *tevuna*, with many more advancements, than the Greeks did with *bina*, yet the Greek philosophers were high intellectual people, because their *midda* was *bina*. Compare the Americans to Aristotle. Even their intellectual people, a scientist, don't compare to a Socrates; they don't even think about him, while he thought about the nature of reality, and Aristotle finally converted. But an American engineer is a *grober mentsh* (a coarse man), totally *grob*.

sensitivity.reason: Calls the American engineer a grober mentsh, a jab at a present-day nation and a profession; also states as fact that Aristotle finally converted, a legend.

sections.title: Leah's heels in Rachel's head: thought becomes a crown for speech (not on tape)
sections.summary: Thought, hidden, becomes a crown for speech, revealed: the letter combinations of thought are the root of speech, and if they stop the speech stops, as "the heel of humility" becomes "the crown of fear". The series has no class on these lines.
